comparator.route: Notarieel Recht, ordinary three-year bachelor; first-listed third-year metajuridical option
comparator.sourceNotes: The accessible September 2026 Dutch faculty OER, Annex VI Article 4 (printed pp.56–57), independently establishes the retained 180-EC Notarial Law structure: 60 EC year-one foundations, 60 EC second-year requirements, and 55 EC third-year requirements plus a restricted 5-EC metajuridical perspective/essay pair. The first-listed criminology option (4+1 EC) remains the neutral selected instance; other paired options are not stacked. The 5-EC thesis requires Academic Language Skills, Academic Skills and Academic Skills II; Private Law precedes Civil Law I/II, Civil Procedure, Business Law and Private International Law, and Criminal (Procedural) Law precedes the two later criminal-law units. The required noncredit first-year Tutoraat remains outside credit totals. The prospective pages are indicative 2027–2028 context, not binding current-year authority. The formerly stored August English EER URL returned 404 in the original audit; its historical availability is unverified, and it is replaced by the accessible current Dutch source and index. The ordinary full-time academic structure is retained; no new assertion about part-time pacing is made. External sources rechecked 2026-10-08; the original UCR no-match judgment and checkedOn date remain unchanged.

alternatives.concept: Study private legal relationships, transnational business law, contracts, economic institutions, corporate finance, taxation and financial governance alongside the public, international and European legal foundations that frame them. This is the closest related-fields response to notarial interests, but it does not teach Dutch family, succession and property law, Dutch tax doctrine, civil procedure or notarial practice.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The route replaces comparative public institutions, conflict and social-movement courses with finance, microeconomics, econometrics and international business governance, a sustained response to private legal and commercial relationships rather than a change of label alone.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic Notarial Law bachelor has a fixed 175-EC compulsory core and one 5-EC restricted third-year choice. The first-listed criminology perspective and its paired essay instantiate that choice without claiming it is mandatory for every student. The full-time three-year presentation avoids treating the separate part-time registration as an academic specialization.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Private law, business and economic governance is the strongest complete related-fields response to the target’s private-law, property, business and taxation orientation. A second public-law direction was tested but would need adjacent conflict, sustainability and general policy courses to reach 24 courses. Dutch family/succession law and notarial taxation cannot form separate routes because UCR lacks their specialist legal subjects and practice sequence. Production stops at one.

notes.text: Radboud Notarial Law is a Dutch-law degree with cumulative civil, family, succession, property-transfer and tax law, civil procedure, notarial professional regulation and a legal thesis. UCR can combine comparative private, business, criminal, constitutional, international and EU law with economics, finance, governance and ethics. These are related-fields programmes, not substitutes for Dutch notarial training or qualification.
